project.name: Meeting Assistant
project.descriptor: A meeting assistant that transcribes audio from meetings, generates structured minutes, tracks action items, and drafts participant-specific emails with mandatory review gates.

requirements.statement: The system must accept audio from virtual sources such as Zoom, Teams, and Meet.
The system must accept audio from physical sources such as room microphones or phone recordings.
The system must flag segments of physical/in-room audio for lower transcription confidence.
The system must tag the output header with meeting type and source.
The system must transcribe audio to text with timestamps.
The system must perform speaker diarization and map speakers to real names if an attendee list is provided.
The system must mark inaudible or uncertain segments as [inaudible] or [unclear — verify].
The system must produce a meeting summary including title, date, time, format, platform/location, attendees, and objective.
The system must summarize key discussion points grouped by topic with timestamp references.
The system must list decisions made with rationale and approver, linked to timestamps.
The system must extract action items into a table format with owner, due date, priority, status, and source timestamp.
The system must propose the next meeting date/time if mentioned and carry over open items.
The system must include a mandatory review gate before drafting participant emails.
The system must draft individualized emails for each participant after Gate #1 approval.
The system must include a mandatory review gate before sending participant emails.
The system must log action items to a tracker with status 'Not Started' after email send confirmation.
The system must compare against prior open items and flag stale items for recurring meetings.
The system must output structured data in JSON format for integration with external trackers.
The system must connect to Microsoft Teams, Zoom, Google Meet, Outlook Calendar, and Trello.

stories.title: Ingest audio from virtual sources
stories.narrative: As a project manager, I want the system to ingest audio from virtual meeting sources like Zoom, Teams, and Meet, so that meetings held on any common platform can be processed without manual file wrangling.
acceptance_criteria: Given a recording from Zoom, Teams, or Meet, when it is submitted, then the system accepts it without manual conversion.

stories.title: Ingest audio from physical sources
stories.narrative: As a project manager, I want the system to ingest audio from physical sources such as room microphones or phone recordings, so that in-person and hybrid meetings are captured too.
acceptance_criteria: Given a room-microphone or phone recording, when it is submitted, then the system accepts it as a valid input source.

stories.title: Flag low-confidence segments in physical audio
stories.narrative: As a project manager, I want low-confidence segments of physical/in-room audio flagged automatically, so that I know which parts of the minutes need a human check.
acceptance_criteria: Given in-room audio with poor signal quality, when it is processed, then the affected segments are flagged for lower confidence.

stories.title: Tag output with meeting type and source
stories.narrative: As a project manager, I want the output header tagged with meeting type and source, so that I can tell at a glance how a transcript was captured.
acceptance_criteria: Given a processed meeting, when the output is generated, then its header states the meeting type and audio source.

stories.title: Ensure idempotency and audit trail for audio ingestion
stories.narrative: As a system auditor, I want idempotency and an audit trail on audio ingestion, so that re-processing the same recording never creates duplicate records and every ingestion is traceable.
acceptance_criteria: Given the same recording submitted twice, when it is ingested the second time, then no duplicate record is created.
Given any ingestion event, when it completes, then it is written to an audit trail.

stories.title: Transcribe audio with timestamps
stories.narrative: As a project manager, I want audio transcribed to text with timestamps, so that every statement in the minutes can be traced back to the moment it was said.
acceptance_criteria: Given an ingested recording, when it is transcribed, then every line of text carries a timestamp.

stories.title: Perform speaker diarization and map speakers
stories.narrative: As a project manager, I want speakers identified and mapped to real names when an attendee list is provided, so that minutes read as a real conversation, not anonymous speaker labels.
acceptance_criteria: Given a transcript and an attendee list, when diarization runs, then speaker turns are mapped to attendee names.

stories.title: Mark inaudible or uncertain segments
stories.narrative: As a project manager, I want inaudible or uncertain segments clearly marked, so that nobody mistakes a guess for a verified statement.
acceptance_criteria: Given a segment the transcriber cannot resolve, when the transcript is produced, then it is marked [inaudible] or [unclear — verify].

stories.title: Generate meeting summary
stories.narrative: As a project manager, I want a meeting summary with title, date, time, format, platform/location, attendees, and objective, so that anyone opening the minutes gets the full context in seconds.
acceptance_criteria: Given a completed transcript, when minutes are generated, then the summary includes title, date, time, format, platform/location, attendees, and objective.

stories.title: Summarize key discussion points
stories.narrative: As a project manager, I want key discussion points summarized and grouped by topic with timestamp references, so that I can review a meeting without listening to the whole recording.
acceptance_criteria: Given a completed transcript, when minutes are generated, then discussion points are grouped by topic with timestamp references.

stories.title: List decisions made with rationale and approver
stories.narrative: As a project manager, I want decisions made in the meeting listed with rationale and approver, linked to timestamps, so that decisions are traceable and defensible later.
acceptance_criteria: Given a completed transcript, when minutes are generated, then each decision lists a rationale, an approver, and a source timestamp.

stories.title: Extract action items into a table format
stories.narrative: As a project manager, I want action items extracted into a table with owner, due date, priority, status, and source timestamp, so that follow-up work doesn't fall through the cracks.
acceptance_criteria: Given a completed transcript, when minutes are generated, then action items appear in a table with owner, due date, priority, status, and source timestamp.

stories.title: Propose next meeting date/time and carry over open items
stories.narrative: As a meeting participant, I want the system to propose the next meeting date/time when mentioned and carry over open items, so that I don't have to manually track what's still outstanding from last time.
acceptance_criteria: Given a next meeting date/time mentioned in the transcript, when minutes are generated, then it is proposed in the output.
Given prior open items, when minutes are generated for a recurring meeting, then unresolved items are carried over.

stories.title: Implement mandatory review gate before email drafting
stories.narrative: As a project manager, I want a mandatory review gate before the system drafts participant emails, so that nothing goes out based on an unverified transcript.
acceptance_criteria: Given generated minutes, when email drafting is requested, then it is blocked until Gate #1 is explicitly approved.

stories.title: Draft individualized emails for participants
stories.narrative: As a project manager, I want individualized emails drafted for each participant after Gate #1 approval, so that each person gets exactly the items relevant to them.
acceptance_criteria: Given Gate #1 approval, when emails are drafted, then each participant receives a draft addressed to their own action items.

stories.title: Implement mandatory review gate before email sending
stories.narrative: As a project manager, I want a mandatory review gate before participant emails are sent, so that I approve the final wording before anything reaches an inbox.
acceptance_criteria: Given drafted emails, when sending is requested, then it is blocked until Gate #2 is explicitly approved.

stories.title: Log action items to tracker after email send confirmation
stories.narrative: As a project manager, I want action items logged to a tracker with status 'Not Started' after email send confirmation, so that tracking only starts once participants have actually been notified.
acceptance_criteria: Given a confirmed email send, when the confirmation is received, then action items are logged to the tracker with status 'Not Started'.

stories.title: Compare against prior open items and flag stale items
stories.narrative: As a project manager, I want the system to compare against prior open items and flag stale ones for recurring meetings, so that old commitments don't quietly disappear.
acceptance_criteria: Given a recurring meeting, when minutes are generated, then items still open past their due date are flagged as stale.

stories.title: Output structured data in JSON format for integration
stories.narrative: As a project manager, I want structured output in JSON format, so that external trackers like Trello can integrate with the meeting data.
acceptance_criteria: Given completed minutes and action items, when output is finalized, then a structured JSON representation is produced for external tracker integration.

guardrails.statement: The system must include a mandatory review gate before drafting participant emails.
The system must include a mandatory review gate before sending participant emails.
